findings.description: No server_side_encryption_configuration block is set, so objects in this bucket are stored unencrypted by default, including the vendor roster object uploaded to it.

findings.issue_category: no ACL / public access controls defined
findings.description: No acl attribute or public access block is defined for this bucket, leaving it to default settings and increasing risk of unintended public exposure compared to explicitly private buckets in the same file.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined for this bucket holding ledger exports, meaning sensitive financial data would be stored unencrypted at rest.
No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined, so model artifacts are stored without encryption at rest.
No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined, leaving operational runbooks (which may contain sensitive operational details) unencrypted at rest.

The acl is set to 'log-delivery-write', which grants the S3 log delivery group write/append access; combined with force_destroy and no bucket policy restricting access further, this widens who can write to the audit trail bucket beyond what may be required.

findings.issue_category: sensitive data uploaded to unencrypted bucket
findings.description: The vendor-roster.xlsx object is uploaded to aws_s3_bucket.reports_archive, which has no server-side encryption configured, so this potentially sensitive vendor data is stored in cleartext at rest.
